rv.q: In this electrifying theatrical experience, at Audible’s Minetta Lane Theater, Quijada and Robinson rely on music made from loops, starting with plucks on the stand-up bass, strums on acoustic guitar and a run on piano keys.

Their extraordinarily edutaining two-person musical Mexodus is likewise adept at multitasking, balancing the past and the present to illuminate a little-known piece of history: how thousands of enslaved Black people in the 19th century fled to Mexico to escape bondage.
It may just be the most fun you have at a show all year.
Mexodus which is quite unusual in form and storytelling is a very powerful musical both because of its excellence, originality and its timeliness.
Quijada and Robinson’s score has the immediate, infectious quality of folk music, but to a hip-hop beat.
These element, combined with highly creative design and David Mendizabal's dynamic staging, make Mexodus one of the most arresting entertainments in town.
If you’re looking for a new musical that will send you into the streets humming, Mexodus is your ticket.
Our collective voice becomes the material for a musical loop, and we are integrated into the final song.

The effect is extraordinary, enabling the pair to make good use of a wide range of instruments — keyboards, guitar, standing bass, accordion, trumpet, percussion, beat-box vocals, and even the call-and-response singing of the audience.
I thought rap lyrics and hip-hop beats would infiltrate subsequent musicals... So it was a delight for me to discover the terrifically entertaining new show Mexodus.
Once the musical architecture locks into place, “the story and the storytelling take over and make Mexodus fly.”
The latest show offered by Audible Theater is more than a play or a musical but might be categorized as an impactful theatrical event.

cn.t: Mexodus earns strong praise for its electrifying two-man performance and innovative live-looping, while illuminating the little-known southward Underground Railroad. Critics call it urgent, edutaining, and a rare theatrical event.

vr.q: It truly cannot be missed... it's absolutely one of those shows you must experience live. So if you're looking for something truly unique to see in new york right now, mexodus is it.
I am not exaggerating when I say I think it is better than most of the shows on Broadway right now.
Brian and Nygel have managed to make a remarkably original, educational, and richly layered piece.
Even with the reservations, I think Mexodus is absolutely worth your time.
I don't think it quite lived up to the hype for me personally but I did still really enjoy it
